source_cards.back: In a push-pull left turn the left hand pulls down to about seven o'clock while the right pushes up to about one o'clock; a right turn mirrors this, with the right hand pulling to about five and the left pushing to about eleven.

source_cards.front: How do you make a hand-over-hand right turn?

source_cards.front: Can an officer stop a driver only for a belt or child restraint violation?
source_cards.back: Tennessee law requires safety belts, child safety seats and booster seats, and an officer may stop and ticket a driver for a belt or child restraint violation alone.

source_cards.front: Who must wear a safety belt whenever the vehicle is moving?
source_cards.back: Every driver and every front-seat passenger must wear a safety belt whenever the vehicle is moving.

source_cards.front: Which back-seat passengers must wear safety belts?
source_cards.back: Back-seat passengers under seventeen years old must also wear safety belts.

source_cards.front: How do the back-seat belt rules change with the driver?
source_cards.back: Back-seat belt rules depend on who is driving: passengers under seventeen must belt in any case, and with a permit or intermediate driver the rule covers back-seat passengers aged four to seventeen.

source_cards.front: What was Tennessee first to pass?
source_cards.back: Tennessee was the first state to pass a Child Passenger Protection Law requiring children to ride in car seats and booster seats.

source_cards.front: Which children must ride in a rear-facing car seat?
source_cards.back: A child under one year old, or any child under twenty pounds, must ride in a rear-facing car seat.

source_cards.front: Which children must ride in a forward-facing car seat?
source_cards.back: A child aged one through three who weighs more than twenty pounds must ride in a forward-facing car seat.

source_cards.front: Which children must ride in a belt-positioning booster seat?
source_cards.back: A child aged four through eight who is shorter than four feet, nine inches must ride in a belt-positioning booster seat while wearing a seat belt.

source_cards.front: How do age and weight decide car seat direction?
source_cards.back: Car seat direction turns on age and weight: rear-facing below one year or twenty pounds, forward-facing from one through three above twenty pounds, then a booster from four through eight while under four feet, nine inches.

source_cards.front: Where must a child in a booster seat ride, and what standards apply?
source_cards.back: A child in a booster seat must ride in the back seat whenever the vehicle has one, and every car seat and booster must meet federal safety standards and be used as its maker and the vehicle maker direct.

source_cards.front: What penalty can follow for not using a required car seat or booster?
source_cards.back: Failing to use a required car seat or booster seat for a child under nine, or one shorter than four feet, nine inches, can be charged as a Class C misdemeanor, with a required class on safely transporting children plus fees and fines.

source_cards.front: How does the plain restraint fine differ from the car seat offense?
source_cards.back: The plain fifty dollars fine applies to a driver who fails to restrain a child under sixteen, while missing a required car seat or booster seat carries the heavier Class C misdemeanor penalty.

source_cards.front: In what five ways do safety belts protect you?
source_cards.back: Safety belts protect in five ways: they prevent ejection, shift crash forces onto the strongest bones, spread forces over a wide area, hold you in driving posture, and protect the head and spinal cord.

source_cards.front: By how much does proper belt use cut front-seat car occupants' risk of death and injury?
source_cards.back: The manual reports that proper lap and shoulder belt use cuts the risk of death for front-seat car occupants by forty-five percent and of moderate-to-critical injury by fifty percent.

source_cards.front: Which single safety behavior contributes to the most traffic deaths?
source_cards.back: According to the manual, not wearing a safety belt contributes to more traffic deaths than any other single safety behavior.

source_cards.front: Is it true that safety belts trap you in a crash?
source_cards.back: The idea that belts trap you is a myth: a belt unbuckles in under a second, and crashes rarely end in fire or deep water.

source_cards.front: Where should the lap belt sit?
source_cards.back: Wear the lap belt low over the pelvis so its lower edge rests snugly on the tops of the thighs.

source_cards.front: Where should the shoulder belt go, and where should it never go?
source_cards.back: The shoulder belt goes over the shoulder and across the chest, never under the arm or across the abdomen, and must not be so loose that it slips off.

source_cards.front: How should a pregnant woman wear her safety belt?
source_cards.back: A pregnant woman should wear the lap belt below her abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

source_cards.front: When is a child big enough for the adult lap and shoulder belt?
source_cards.back: A child is big enough for the adult lap and shoulder belt once they can sit with their back against the seat back and their knees bend over the seat edge.

source_cards.front: How should the belts fit a child using adult belts?
source_cards.back: On a child, the lap belt should sit low and snug on the upper thighs and the shoulder belt should cross the chest between neck and shoulder, never behind the back or under the arm.

source_cards.front: What is the belts-to-bones rule for children?
source_cards.back: Under the belts-to-bones rule the pelvis and collarbone should take the belt's pressure, so if the belt rides on the stomach or crosses the face or neck, the child goes back to a booster seat.

source_cards.front: Where should the lap belt sit on a child using vehicle safety belts?
source_cards.back: Once a child transitions out of a safety seat to vehicle belts, position the lap belt firmly across the upper thighs so it stays low and snug over the hips.

source_cards.front: How well do child safety seats help infants and toddlers survive?
source_cards.back: The manual says infants properly secured in safety seats survive almost seventy-five percent of crashes that would otherwise kill them, and toddlers survive more than half.

source_cards.front: How many child passenger deaths could correct restraint use prevent?
source_cards.back: The manual states that correct use of child restraints could prevent nine of ten deaths and eight of ten serious injuries among child passengers under four.

source_cards.front: How do air bags work best?
source_cards.back: Air bags work best combined with safety belts, which together are the best protection available in a car, SUV or truck.

source_cards.front: Where should a child safety seat not be placed?
source_cards.back: Do not put a child safety seat in the front seat of a car with a passenger air bag; place it in a rear seat if one exists.

source_cards.front: Where do infants in rear-facing seats belong in a car with a passenger air bag?
source_cards.back: Infants in rear-facing seats belong in the rear seat of a vehicle that has a passenger air bag, if a rear seat is available.

source_cards.front: How far should an adult sit from the air bag cover?
source_cards.back: Adults should always wear both lap and shoulder belts and sit far enough back to leave ten to twelve inches between the chest and the air bag cover, as NHTSA recommends.

source_cards.front: What does a red ALL WAY plate under a stop sign mean?
source_cards.back: A red ALL WAY plate under a stop sign means every direction of traffic at that intersection must stop.

source_cards.front: What does a diamond sign drawn as a small road map show?
source_cards.back: A diamond warning sign drawn as a small road map shows the kind of intersection ahead, such as a crossroad.

source_cards.front: What do the T-intersection sign and chevron signs mean?
source_cards.back: A T-intersection sign means you must turn right or left ahead and be prepared to yield, while chevron signs emphasize a sharp change in direction.

source_cards.front: How are no-passing zones set?
source_cards.back: No-passing zones are set by how far ahead you can see, allowing for hidden hazards such as hills, curves, intersections and driveways.

source_cards.front: What should you do at a yellow light?
source_cards.back: A yellow light means red comes next: slow to a smooth stop if you safely can, never speed up to beat it, and if you are already in the intersection keep going carefully.

source_cards.front: What does a green light allow, and whom must you still yield to?
source_cards.back: A green light lets you go only if the intersection is clear: yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in it, and to oncoming traffic when turning left.

source_cards.front: Why should you not pull into a busy intersection before your path is clear?
source_cards.back: Do not pull into a busy intersection to turn until your path is clear, or you may be stranded inside it.

source_cards.front: What does a green turn arrow give you?
source_cards.back: With a green turn arrow you have the right-of-way to turn only that way, after yielding to anyone already in the intersection.

source_cards.front: What do yellow and red turn arrows mean?
source_cards.back: A yellow turn arrow means get ready to yield to oncoming traffic, and a red arrow or red light in your lane bans all turns even when other lanes have green.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow arrow allow?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after yielding to all oncoming traffic and to bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk.

source_cards.front: How does Tennessee law treat an intersection whose signal is not working?
source_cards.back: When a traffic signal is not working, Tennessee law treats the intersection as an all-way stop.

source_cards.front: Who yields when two vehicles stop at an all-way stop at the same moment?
source_cards.back: When two or more vehicles stop at an all-way stop at the same moment, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

source_cards.front: To which pedestrians must you yield at crosswalks?
source_cards.back: Yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or about to enter it, and remember that not every crosswalk is marked.

source_cards.front: What must you do at a steady red light, and when may you turn right?
source_cards.back: On a steady red, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line; unless a sign forbids it, you may then turn right once no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

source_cards.front: What do the edge line colors tell you about your direction?
source_cards.back: A solid white line marks the right edge of your lane, and a yellow line marks the left edge of lanes going your direction, so yellow on your right and white on your left means you are going the wrong way.

source_cards.front: When may you cross a broken yellow center line?
source_cards.back: A broken yellow center line may be crossed to pass when no traffic is coming and it is safe.

source_cards.front: May you pass across double solid yellow lines?
source_cards.back: Double solid yellow lines may not be crossed to pass from either direction, though you may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road when safe.

source_cards.front: With one solid and one broken yellow line, when may you pass?
source_cards.back: With one solid and one broken yellow line, you may pass only when the broken line is on your side, and you must be back in your lane before the passing zone ends.

source_cards.front: What do broken, solid and double solid white lines mean?
source_cards.back: White lines separate lanes going the same way: a broken white line may be crossed when safe, a solid white line means stay in your lane, and a double solid white line must not be crossed.

source_cards.front: Where should you stop when there is a stop line, a crosswalk, or neither?
source_cards.back: Stop behind a painted stop line; with no stop line, stop before the first crosswalk line, and with neither, stop before your front bumper crosses the cross street's edge line.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow arrow allow?

source_cards.front: How does Tennessee law define a pedestrian?

source_cards.front: What should a pedestrian who started on WALK do?

source_cards.front: To which pedestrians must you yield at crosswalks?

source_cards.front: Why should you never try to beat a train?
source_cards.back: Never try to beat a train, because drivers usually misjudge its speed, and the manual counts more than two hundred crashes a year at railroad crossings.

source_cards.front: What does the X-shaped crossbuck mark?
source_cards.back: The X-shaped crossbuck stands at every railroad grade crossing and marks exactly where the tracks are, with a small sign below showing how many tracks there are.

source_cards.front: What must you do at a railroad crossing with gates?
source_cards.back: Where a crossing has gates, stop when the lights start flashing and before the gate comes down, and wait until the gates rise and the lights stop.

source_cards.front: What does a white crossbuck with RR painted on the pavement warn of?

source_cards.back: Every sign's shape and color announce its purpose, so a stop sign hidden by dirt, branches or snow is still known by its red octagon.

source_cards.front: Which signs use a red background?
source_cards.back: Red is the background only for stop signs, the four-way or all-way plates beneath them, do not enter and wrong way signs, and interstate route markers.

source_cards.front: What do yellow, brown, green and blue sign backgrounds mean?
source_cards.back: Yellow is the background for general warning signs, brown marks recreational and cultural points of interest, green is for guide signs and mileposts, and blue is for motorist services.

source_cards.front: Which colors are used for sign messages and legends?
source_cards.back: Black is used for regulatory signs and for the message on white, yellow and orange signs, while white also serves as the lettering on brown, green, blue, black and red signs.

source_cards.front: What shape and color is a stop sign, and what does it require?
source_cards.back: The octagon is the only eight-sided sign, always red with white letters, and requires a complete stop without passing the crosswalk.

source_cards.front: What should you do if you cannot see cross traffic after stopping at a stop sign?
source_cards.back: If you cannot see cross traffic after stopping at a stop sign, creep forward carefully to where you can see and go only when it is safe.

source_cards.front: What does a red ALL WAY plate under a stop sign mean?
source_cards.back: A red ALL WAY plate under a stop sign means every direction of traffic at that intersection must stop.

source_cards.front: What must you do at a yield sign?
source_cards.back: At a triangular yield sign, slow down and stop for cross traffic coming from either side; with no cars coming you may enter carefully without a full stop, but always stop in heavy traffic.

source_cards.front: What does the round railroad advance sign warn of?
source_cards.back: The round railroad advance sign warns that a grade crossing is ahead, so slow down and be ready to stop if a train is coming.

source_cards.front: What does the X-shaped crossbuck mark?
source_cards.back: The X-shaped crossbuck stands at every railroad grade crossing and marks exactly where the tracks are, with a small sign below showing how many tracks there are.

source_cards.front: What do flashing lights on a crossbuck mean?
source_cards.back: Flashing lights on a crossbuck mean a train is coming: stop, stay stopped until it passes, and make sure every track is clear before crossing.

source_cards.front: What does a white crossbuck with RR painted on the pavement warn of?
source_cards.back: A white crossbuck with the letters RR painted on the pavement warns of many railroad crossings ahead.

source_cards.front: What do diamond-shaped signs warn about?
source_cards.back: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards or unexpected conditions ahead and usually call for slowing down.

source_cards.front: What does a diamond sign drawn as a small road map show?
source_cards.back: A diamond warning sign drawn as a small road map shows the kind of intersection ahead, such as a crossroad.

source_cards.front: What does a small advisory speed plate under a warning sign give?
source_cards.back: A small advisory speed plate under a warning sign gives the recommended top safe speed for that hazard.

source_cards.front: What do stop-ahead and yield-ahead signs warn of?
source_cards.back: Stop-ahead and yield-ahead signs warn of a stop or yield sign you cannot yet see, and you should begin slowing when you pass them; a traffic-light symbol version warns of a signal ahead.

source_cards.front: What should you do at a lane-ends sign and at a merging-traffic sign?
source_cards.back: At a lane-ends sign, signal and merge into the remaining lane, and at a merging-traffic sign, check behind you and move over if you can to give merging drivers room.

source_cards.front: What does a narrow bridge sign warn?
source_cards.back: A narrow bridge sign warns that the bridge may force passing cars to slow down.

source_cards.front: What do the T-intersection sign and chevron signs mean?
source_cards.back: A T-intersection sign means you must turn right or left ahead and be prepared to yield, while chevron signs emphasize a sharp change in direction.

source_cards.front: What can speed signs show?
source_cards.back: Speed signs show the maximum allowed, the minimum required or a coming change in the limit.

source_cards.front: What does the keep-right sign mean on a road with more than one lane each way?
source_cards.back: On a road with more than one lane each way, the keep-right sign means stay in the far right lane unless passing a slower car or turning left.

source_cards.front: What does a red circle with a diagonal line mean?
source_cards.back: A red circle with a diagonal line on a white sign means the action pictured behind it is forbidden.

source_cards.front: What do work zone signs usually look like and warn about?
source_cards.back: Work zone signs are usually orange diamonds or rectangles with black letters or symbols, warning of workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment and lane closures.

source_cards.front: What do the arrows and must-exit marking on interstate guide signs mean?
source_cards.back: On interstate guide signs the arrows point to the lane you need to enter or leave the highway, and when a guide sign carries the must-exit marking, every vehicle in the lanes under those arrows must exit.

source_cards.front: What do flashing red and flashing yellow lights mean?
source_cards.back: A flashing red light is the same as a stop sign, and a flashing yellow light means slow down and go through carefully.

source_cards.front: How does Tennessee law treat an intersection whose signal is not working?

source_cards.front: Where are lane control signals over each lane mostly used?
source_cards.back: Lane control signals over each lane are mostly used where traffic direction changes by time of day, and they also show whether toll plaza lanes are open.

source_cards.front: When must you yield to a metro transit bus?
source_cards.back: Yield to a metro transit bus that has signaled and is pulling back into traffic from a bus stop.

source_cards.front: Which lanes should you turn from and into?

source_cards.front: Whom must you yield to when turning left or leaving a driveway?
source_cards.back: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and when entering from a driveway or alley, yield to all traffic on the main road.

source_cards.back: Stopping distance depends on the pavement, tires, brakes, shock absorbers and the vehicle's weight when loaded or towing.

source_cards.back: Tennessee law sets a fine of at least two hundred fifty dollars and up to five hundred dollars for speeding in an active work zone.

source_cards.front: What counts as a work zone, and how is it marked?
source_cards.back: Work zones include utility work, tree trimming and surveying, and are marked by orange or yellow-green signs, flashing equipment lights and brightly dressed workers.

source_cards.front: What do the manual's work zone crash figures show?
source_cards.back: The manual reports that Tennessee work zone crashes in two thousand twenty-one killed twenty-six people, injured one thousand one hundred five and caused three thousand ten property damage cases.

source_cards.front: Whose stop signals at construction sites must you obey?
source_cards.back: You must stop completely when a flagger at a construction site or a police officer signals you to stop.

source_cards.front: When must trains sound their horn, and what signs mean do not cross?
source_cards.back: Trains must sound their horn about one thousand five hundred feet before a crossing, and flashing lights, a lowered gate, a flagger or a visible train all mean you must not cross.

source_cards.front: Who may use a reserved lane marked with a white diamond?
source_cards.back: Reserved lanes marked by a white diamond are for buses, bicycles or HOV car pools only, though you may cross one to turn within the next half block.

source_cards.front: Where must you never pass on the right?
source_cards.back: Never pass on the right in a bike lane, a parking lane, or an emergency lane within sight of a signal or stop sign; the driver passing on the right is at fault if the car ahead turns right.

source_cards.front: How much space does Tennessee law require when passing a bicycle?
source_cards.back: Tennessee law requires at least three feet of space when passing a bicycle going your way, kept until you are safely past.

source_cards.front: How should you pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road?
source_cards.back: Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, and do not pass where it would squeeze the rider toward parked cars.

source_cards.front: Is walking on an interstate legal?

source_cards.front: When should you signal if you plan to turn just past an intersection?
source_cards.back: If you plan to turn just past an intersection, wait until you are in the intersection to signal, so no one thinks you are turning at it.

source_cards.front: When should you move into the turn lane and choose your gear?
source_cards.back: Move into the correct turn lane as early as possible, sooner on faster roads, choose your gear before the intersection and accelerate slightly through the turn.

source_cards.front: When should you not enter an intersection to turn?
source_cards.back: Do not enter an intersection to turn if traffic ahead could keep you from finishing the turn before the light changes; wait behind the stop line.

source_cards.front: What should you do if you are in the wrong lane for a turn?
source_cards.back: If you are in the wrong lane for a turn, go on to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.

source_cards.front: What should you not do during the turn itself?
source_cards.back: Do not brake or press the clutch during the turn itself, and do not shift gears in the intersection.

source_cards.front: How do two drivers turning left from opposite directions pass each other?
source_cards.back: When two drivers meet at an intersection and both turn left, each turns to the left of the other.

source_cards.front: When should you start turning the wheel in a left turn?
source_cards.back: In a left turn, keep the wheels straight until you reach the turn point, just before the imaginary center of the intersection.

source_cards.front: What should you do if the light turns yellow while you wait to turn left?
source_cards.back: If the light turns yellow while you are waiting to turn left, do not pull into the intersection.

source_cards.front: Which lane do you enter turning left from a one-way onto a two-way street?
source_cards.back: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, enter the intersection before turning sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line, and move right only after signaling and checking.

source_cards.front: What do white channel lines in an intersection do?
source_cards.back: White channel lines and arrows in an intersection guide you into the correct lane as you turn.

source_cards.front: Which way do you travel in a roundabout, and whom do you yield to?
source_cards.back: Always travel counterclockwise, to the right, around a roundabout, and yield to vehicles already circulating before entering.

source_cards.front: What should you watch for in a multi-lane roundabout?
source_cards.back: In a multi-lane roundabout be ready to yield to vehicles crossing in front of you from the inside lane to exit, and go around again if you miss your street.

source_cards.front: Where may you not make a U-turn?
source_cards.back: You may not make a U-turn at an intersection controlled by a signal or officer, or anywhere you cannot see five hundred feet of traffic both ways.

source_cards.front: Where else are U-turns banned?
source_cards.back: U-turns are also banned between intersections in a city and wherever signs or markings forbid them; driving around the block is safer.

source_cards.front: Which side of a divided highway must you use, and where may you cross?
source_cards.back: On a divided highway always use the road on the right, and cross the median only at an authorized crossover or intersection or when directed.

source_cards.front: What does a lane with both turn and straight arrows allow?
source_cards.back: A lane with both a turn arrow and a straight arrow lets you go either way, following normal right-of-way rules unless a protected arrow is showing.

source_cards.front: Who has the right-of-way when two drivers enter a shared center turn lane?
source_cards.back: When drivers from opposite directions enter a shared center turn lane, the first one in has the right-of-way.

source_cards.front: How should you use a shared center turn lane?
source_cards.back: Enter a shared center turn lane just before your turn, never ride in it to reach a turn lane at the next intersection, and you may use it to wait before merging right from a side street.

source_cards.front: Where should you not pass?
source_cards.back: Do not pass near an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, or when approaching a hill or curve.

source_cards.front: May you cross a solid yellow line to turn left in a no-passing zone?
source_cards.back: In a no-passing zone you may still cross the solid yellow line to turn left into or out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway.

source_cards.front: Where is backing illegal?
source_cards.back: Backing from a driveway into an intersection is illegal, and so is backing up on an interstate.

source_cards.front: Name other places where parking is illegal.
source_cards.back: Parking is also illegal in front of a driveway, in an intersection or fire lane, on a sidewalk, bridge or tunnel, on interstate ramps unless disabled, and on an interstate shoulder except in an emergency.

source_cards.front: What passing moves are banned on shoulders and between lanes?

source_cards.front: Where is backing illegal?

source_cards.back: To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, bumpers even, no closer than two feet, then back slowly with the wheel turned sharply right to about a forty-five-degree angle.

source_cards.front: How close to the curb should a finished parallel park be?
source_cards.back: A finished parallel park should leave you no more than eighteen inches from the curb, and check traffic before opening the driver's door.

source_cards.front: Why are roundabouts used?
source_cards.back: Roundabouts are used to slow traffic, cut crashes and discourage commuters from cutting through neighborhoods.

source_cards.front: Which side of the splitter island do you keep to, and may you stop inside a roundabout?

source_cards.back: Passing a truck takes longer on level ground, is easier on an upgrade where it slows, and may need more speed on a downgrade, but you still may not exceed the limit.

source_cards.back: While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight, because a rear-end hit with the wheels turned can push you into oncoming traffic.

source_cards.front: What should you do if the light turns yellow while you wait to turn left?
source_cards.back: If the light turns yellow while you are waiting to turn left, do not pull into the intersection.

source_cards.front: Which lane do you enter when turning left onto a one-way street?
source_cards.back: Turning left onto a one-way street, turn sharply into the first lane, the one nearest the left curb.

source_cards.front: Which lane should you approach a left turn from on a one-way street?
source_cards.back: On a one-way street, approach a left turn from the lane farthest to the left.

source_cards.front: Which lane must you use where a lane is marked for left turns?
source_cards.back: Where a lane is marked for left turns, turn only from that lane, and in multiple turn lanes stay in your starting lane all the way through.

source_cards.front: Which lane do you enter turning left from a one-way onto a two-way street?
source_cards.back: Turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, enter the intersection before turning sharply into the first lane right of the yellow line, and move right only after signaling and checking.

source_cards.front: May you turn left on red from a one-way street onto a two-way street?

source_cards.front: When may you turn left on red from one one-way street onto another?
source_cards.back: Turning left from one one-way street onto another, you may go on red after a full stop unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

source_cards.front: Which turns on red does Tennessee allow?
source_cards.back: Tennessee allows a right turn on red, and a left turn on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street going left, unless a sign forbids it, after a full stop and yielding.

source_cards.front: When may the second lane of a multiple turn lane make the same turn?
source_cards.back: In a multiple turn lane setup, the second lane may make the same turn as the first only when a sign or pavement marking allows it.

source_cards.front: How should you make a right turn?
source_cards.back: On a right turn, do not swing wide to the left; stay close to the right curb and turn into the lane nearest the right curb.

source_cards.front: What can happen if you swing wide before a right turn?
source_cards.back: If you swing wide before a right turn, the driver behind may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right.

source_cards.front: What should you check before a right turn?
source_cards.back: Before a right turn, look left and right for cross traffic and for oncoming vehicles also turning, and check for pedestrians and bicyclists.

source_cards.front: Why should you never pass a truck on the right if it may turn right?

source_cards.front: Where may you not make a U-turn?

source_cards.front: Where else are U-turns banned?
source_cards.back: U-turns are also banned between intersections in a city and wherever signs or markings forbid them; driving around the block is safer.

source_cards.front: Can towns ban U-turns entirely?
source_cards.back: Some towns and cities ban U-turns on their streets entirely, so check with local police.

source_cards.front: Are U-turns legal on interstates, and who may use median crossovers?
source_cards.back: U-turns on interstates are illegal, and median emergency crossovers are only for emergency and maintenance vehicles.

source_cards.front: When may you drive left of center?
source_cards.back: Drive left of center only to pass, to get around an obstruction, on a one-way road or to turn left, and go around crashes to the right when possible.

source_cards.front: What is a shared center turn lane for, and how far may you drive in it?
source_cards.back: A shared center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction, may not be used for passing, and may not be driven in for more than three hundred feet.

source_cards.front: Who has the right-of-way when two drivers enter a shared center turn lane?
source_cards.back: When drivers from opposite directions enter a shared center turn lane, the first one in has the right-of-way.

source_cards.front: How should you use a shared center turn lane?
source_cards.back: Enter a shared center turn lane just before your turn, never ride in it to reach a turn lane at the next intersection, and you may use it to wait before merging right from a side street.

source_cards.front: When may you pass on the right?

source_cards.back: Vehicles that run out of gas or break down from poor maintenance can cause bottlenecks, so watch your fuel and maintain your car.

source_cards.front: How should you signal for help after a breakdown?
source_cards.back: If your car breaks down and you need help, raise the hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or antenna, and if possible wait in or near the car on the side away from traffic.

source_cards.front: Why should you stay with your vehicle after a breakdown?
source_cards.back: Walking along the interstate is dangerous, so keep children away from traffic, and a passing officer not on another call will stop to help a driver who stays with the vehicle.

source_cards.front: Who may use the HOV lane during peak hours?
source_cards.back: During the morning peak of seven to nine a.m. and the evening peak of four to six p.m., the HOV lane is reserved for vehicles with two or more people, motorcycles, buses and emergency vehicles.

source_cards.front: What does the Move Over Law require?
source_cards.back: The Move Over Law requires you to leave an empty lane next to a stopped emergency, utility, maintenance or recovery vehicle with flashing lights on an interstate or other highway with two or more lanes your way.

source_cards.front: Does the Move Over rule cover ordinary cars with flashing lights?

source_cards.back: If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, have a mechanic check the shocks and suspension.

source_cards.front: Why read your owner's manual about brakes?
source_cards.back: Read your vehicle owner's manual to learn how its antilock braking system works, since antilock brakes let you stop without skidding.

source_cards.front: How do you stop quickly without antilock brakes?
source_cards.back: To stop quickly without antilock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, since braking too hard or too long can cause a skid.

source_cards.front: Without antilock brakes, what do you do if the wheels lock?
source_cards.back: Without antilock brakes, if the wheels lock and you feel a skid, let up on the pedal quickly, then press down again once the skid stops, repeating until the car stops.

source_cards.front: How do antilock brakes change an emergency stop?
source_cards.back: In an emergency with antilock brakes the wheels do not lock and the car can still be steered, while without them all wheels may lock and the skidding car cannot be steered properly.

source_cards.front: Can you steer while braking with antilock brakes?
source_cards.back: With antilock brakes you can steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must swerve and stop or slow quickly.

source_cards.front: How hard should you brake for an animal with no one close behind?
source_cards.back: If no vehicle is close behind you, brake hard for an animal but do not lock the wheels into a skid.

source_cards.front: What can worn or bald tires do?
source_cards.back: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder on wet roads, raise the chance of a flat and can cause hydroplaning.

source_cards.back: For a quick evasive turn to the left, the right hand swings from three o'clock toward nine o'clock as far as needed while the left hand slides toward the bottom of the wheel to steady the grip.

source_cards.front: How do you regain your lane after clearing a hazard?
source_cards.back: As you clear the hazard, turn the wheel back to the right to regain your lane, then left just enough to straighten out, returning your hands to nine and three; for a quick right turn, mirror every step.

source_cards.front: What are the most common car-bicycle crashes?
source_cards.back: The most common car-bicycle crashes happen when a driver turns left in front of an oncoming bicycle or turns right across a bicycle's path.

source_cards.front: What should you do when turning near a bicyclist?
source_cards.back: When turning left with a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction, wait for the rider to pass; when turning right with a bicyclist approaching on your right, let the rider through first.

source_cards.front: What rights do bicyclists have, and where are they banned?
source_cards.back: On most roads bicyclists have the same rights and duties as other road users, but they are banned from limited-access highways, expressways and certain marked roads.

source_cards.front: Where must bicyclists ride?
source_cards.back: Bicyclists must ride on the right side of the road in the same direction as traffic, as far right as practical while avoiding hazards.

source_cards.front: Why may a bicyclist ride toward the center of the lane?
source_cards.back: When a bicyclist rides away from parked cars toward the center of the lane, the rider is riding properly to avoid opening doors.

source_cards.front: How much room must you give when passing a bicycle?
source_cards.back: Tennessee law requires you to pass a bicycle going your way slowly and with at least three feet of clearance, keeping that space until you are safely past.

source_cards.front: May you pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic?
source_cards.back: Never pass between a bicyclist and oncoming traffic on a two-lane road; slow down and wait until it is safe.

source_cards.front: How should you share a turn lane with a bicyclist?
source_cards.back: If you share a left turn lane with a bicyclist, stay behind the rider until the turn is complete, and before a right turn merge with bicycle traffic rather than cutting across it.

source_cards.front: Where should you never pass a bicycle?
source_cards.back: Never pass a bicycle where the street is too narrow or the pass would push the rider close to parked cars.

source_cards.front: How should you use the horn before passing a bicyclist?
source_cards.back: Before passing a bicycle on a narrow road when the rider may not know you are there, tap the horn gently and briefly instead of blasting it.

source_cards.front: May drivers use a bicycle-only lane to turn or park?
source_cards.back: A marked and signed bicycle-only lane must never be used by drivers for turning, passing or parking.

source_cards.front: Which beams should you use for an oncoming bicyclist at night?
source_cards.back: At night, do not use your high beams when you see an oncoming bicyclist.

source_cards.front: When may a bicyclist take the full lane?
source_cards.back: A bicyclist may take the full lane when passing another vehicle, when the road has hazards such as potholes, debris or parked cars, or when the lane is too narrow to share.

source_cards.front: Which habits keep bicyclists safe?
source_cards.back: Bicyclists should wear a helmet, never slip between a truck or bus and the curb, and ride on the right with the flow of traffic.

source_cards.front: What lights must a bicycle have at night?
source_cards.back: Tennessee law requires a bicycle ridden at night to have a front lamp showing white light visible for at least five hundred feet and a red reflector or red lamp visible from five hundred feet behind.

source_cards.front: What should you expect from children on bicycles?
source_cards.back: Children on bicycles cannot judge traffic well, so expect erratic moves and sudden turns wherever children may be riding.

source_cards.front: Where can bicycles appear suddenly?
source_cards.back: Watch for bicycles coming out of driveways or from behind parked cars and other obstructions.

source_cards.front: What does a pennant flag on a bicycle often mean?
source_cards.back: A red or orange pennant flag on a bicycle commonly means the rider has impaired hearing, so slow down.

source_cards.front: What is the stop or slow hand signal?
source_cards.back: The hand signal for stopping or slowing is an arm held out and bent downward at the elbow, with the palm facing back.

source_cards.back: Pedestrians generally have the right-of-way at all intersections, and every intersection has a crosswalk even when no lines are painted.

source_cards.front: What care must drivers always use around pedestrians?
source_cards.back: Whatever the right-of-way rules say, the law requires drivers to use great care and extreme caution to avoid hitting pedestrians.

source_cards.front: When must you yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk?
source_cards.back: Yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk who is on your half of the road, or so close to it from the other half as to be in danger.

source_cards.front: Whom must you yield to when crossing a sidewalk at a driveway?
source_cards.back: Yield to people on the sidewalk when you enter or leave a driveway, alley, parking lot or garage across it, and never honk or rev your engine to rush a pedestrian.

source_cards.front: What must you do for a crossing pedestrian in a flashing school zone?
source_cards.back: In a marked school zone with its warning flashers on, you must stop for a pedestrian crossing in a marked crosswalk or at an intersection without one, and stay stopped until the pedestrian has crossed your roadway.

source_cards.front: Whom must you always yield to with a cane or guide dog?
source_cards.back: Always yield to a blind pedestrian carrying a white or metallic cane with a red tip or using a guide dog.

source_cards.front: What should you wait for at intersections with a motorcycle?
source_cards.back: At intersections, where most motorcycle crashes happen, wait until the rider's intention to turn or go straight is clear before pulling into the rider's path.

source_cards.front: Why must drivers always yield to trains?
source_cards.back: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to trains, because a train cannot stop quickly; one going fifty-five miles per hour needs a full mile to stop.

source_cards.back: After passing a truck, do not move back in front of it until you can see the whole front of the truck in your rearview mirror, and do not slow down once you are ahead.

source_cards.front: Where are a truck's blind spots?

source_cards.front: Why never cross behind a truck about to back up?

source_cards.front: How do recreational vehicles handle?
source_cards.back: Recreational vehicles handle more like large trucks, need longer stopping distances and have many blind spots.

source_cards.front: Why are motorcycles hard to see and judge?
source_cards.back: A motorcycle's narrow, short profile makes it harder to see and makes its distance and speed harder to judge.

source_cards.front: What causes most car-motorcycle crashes?
source_cards.back: Research shows two-thirds of car-motorcycle crashes are caused by the car driver turning in front of the motorcycle, often without ever seeing it.

source_cards.front: May you share a lane with a motorcycle?
source_cards.back: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, so never try to share a lane with one.

source_cards.front: How should you pass a motorcycle?
source_cards.back: Pass a motorcycle as you would a car, but not too close or too fast, because the blast of air can push the rider out of control.

source_cards.front: How far should you follow a motorcycle?
source_cards.back: Allow at least a two-second following distance behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to maneuver or stop.

source_cards.front: Why check blind spots for motorcycles before changing lanes?
source_cards.back: Motorcyclists riding alongside a lane of cars are often out of view, so check your blind spots before changing lanes.

source_cards.front: What should you wait for at intersections with a motorcycle?
source_cards.back: At intersections, where most motorcycle crashes happen, wait until the rider's intention to turn or go straight is clear before pulling into the rider's path.

source_cards.front: Why are motorcycles hard to judge at night?
source_cards.back: At night a motorcycle's single headlight or taillight can blend with other lights and make its distance hard to judge, so dim your high beams for it as for any vehicle.

source_cards.front: Which road conditions trouble motorcyclists most?
source_cards.back: Wet roads, crosswinds, truck wind blasts, railroad crossings and metal grated bridges all cause extra trouble for motorcyclists, so give them more room.

source_cards.front: Which vehicles accelerate fastest and slowest?
source_cards.back: Motorcycles accelerate faster than any other vehicle, while trucks and buses are the slowest.

source_cards.front: How do trucks make right turns?
source_cards.back: Trucks must swing wide to the left to make a right turn, and they cannot see cars or motorcycles directly behind or beside them.

source_cards.front: What should you do after passing a truck downhill?

source_cards.front: Who are the most frequent victims of car-pedestrian crashes?
source_cards.back: Young, elderly, disabled and intoxicated pedestrians are the most frequent victims of car-pedestrian crashes, so watch for them especially.

source_cards.front: Which pedestrians are least predictable?
source_cards.back: Children are the least predictable and hardest-to-see pedestrians, so take extra care near school zones, bus stops, playgrounds, parks and snack vendors.

source_cards.front: Whom must you yield to when crossing a sidewalk at a driveway?

source_cards.back: Where sidewalks exist, pedestrians must use them, and walking in the road there is illegal.

source_cards.front: How should a pedestrian look before crossing?
source_cards.back: Before crossing, stop at the curb or road edge and look left, right and left again, then check over your shoulder for turning vehicles.

source_cards.front: Why step back at corners when trucks turn?
source_cards.back: Trucks and buses make wide right turns that can run up onto the corner of the sidewalk, so pedestrians on corners should step back.

source_cards.front: How can pedestrians be seen at night?
source_cards.back: At night, pedestrians should wear bright or reflective clothing, and carrying a flashlight is the safest way to be seen.

source_cards.front: When may pedestrians not cross?
source_cards.back: Pedestrians may not cross on a red or yellow light, or on a mixed red and green turn light, unless facing a WALK signal.

source_cards.front: Why not step out in front of a close vehicle?
source_cards.back: Pedestrians must not step off the curb into the path of a vehicle so close that it is an immediate hazard, because vehicles cannot stop at once.

source_cards.front: Who are most children killed in school bus crashes?
source_cards.back: Most children killed in school bus crashes are pedestrians aged five to seven, hit by the bus or by drivers illegally passing a stopped school bus.

source_cards.front: When do most school bus pedestrian deaths happen?
source_cards.back: Nearly three of every four school bus pedestrian deaths happen while children are getting on or off the bus.

source_cards.front: How much do communities depend on trucks?
source_cards.back: Trucks are the only delivery and pickup method for about seventy-seven percent of America's communities, and a tractor-trailer combination can be longer than seventy feet.

source_cards.front: How do trucks make right turns?

source_cards.front: What can cutting in front of a truck force?

source_cards.front: When can you move back in front of a truck you passed?

source_cards.front: How should you exit near a truck?
source_cards.back: Do not drive directly behind a truck or bus, and if you are exiting, slow down and exit behind the truck instead of cutting in front of it.

source_cards.front: Why do trucks often seem slower than they are?
source_cards.back: Because of their size, trucks and buses often look slower than they really are.

source_cards.front: What does a trucker's headlight blink after you pass mean?
source_cards.back: If a truck or bus driver blinks the headlights after you pass, it signals that you may move back in, once you can see the truck's front in your mirror.

source_cards.front: Which lane should you avoid near a weigh station?
source_cards.back: Avoid the right lane near a commercial vehicle weigh station so slow trucks can merge back onto the road.

source_cards.front: Where should you wait behind a truck on an uphill grade?
source_cards.back: On an uphill grade, keep to the left side of your lane while waiting behind a truck so its driver can see you, and leave extra room in case it rolls back.

source_cards.front: What should you do while a truck passes you?
source_cards.back: When a truck passes you, keep to the far side of your lane and slow slightly, and never speed up while a truck or bus is passing.

source_cards.front: How should you position yourself when meeting a truck?
source_cards.back: When meeting a truck from the opposite direction, keep as far right as you can, because the wind turbulence between vehicles pushes them apart.

source_cards.front: What should you do after passing a truck downhill?
source_cards.back: Trucks lose speed climbing hills but travel faster downhill, so after passing one on a downgrade keep your speed instead of slowing in front of it.

source_cards.front: What should you do about truck spray in rain?
source_cards.back: In rain or standing water, a truck's spray can badly cut your vision, so move as far from it as you can within your lane.

source_cards.front: Why never cross behind a truck about to back up?
source_cards.back: Never cross behind a truck that is getting ready to back up, since you will be in the driver's blind spots.

source_cards.front: May you stop in a runaway truck ramp?
source_cards.back: Never stop or park in a runaway truck ramp, which exists to stop out-of-control trucks and buses on steep downgrades.

source_cards.front: How much deadlier is a train crash than a car crash?
source_cards.back: Your chance of dying in a crash with a train is about thirty times higher than in a crash with a car or even a large truck.

source_cards.front: Which vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing?
source_cards.back: School buses, passenger buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop at every railroad crossing, and you must never pass them there on a two-way road.

source_cards.front: When may you pass a bus stopped at a multi-lane crossing?
source_cards.back: On a multi-lane road, do not pass a bus or hazardous materials truck stopped at a crossing unless the crossing's signals or gates are clearly not activated.

source_cards.front: How do recreational vehicles handle?
source_cards.back: Recreational vehicles handle more like large trucks, need longer stopping distances and have many blind spots.

source_cards.front: Where should you watch for pedestrians when turning right?
source_cards.back: Watch for pedestrians on your right, especially when you are making a right turn.

source_cards.front: What should you do when turning near a bicyclist?
source_cards.back: When turning left with a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction, wait for the rider to pass; when turning right with a bicyclist approaching on your right, let the rider through first.

source_cards.front: How should you share a turn lane with a bicyclist?
source_cards.back: If you share a left turn lane with a bicyclist, stay behind the rider until the turn is complete, and before a right turn merge with bicycle traffic rather than cutting across it.

source_cards.front: What are the turn hand signals?
source_cards.back: Hand signals: a left turn is the left arm straight out, and a right turn is the left arm bent up at the elbow or the right arm straight out.

source_cards.front: How do trucks make right turns?
source_cards.back: Trucks must swing wide to the left to make a right turn, and they cannot see cars or motorcycles directly behind or beside them.

source_cards.front: How does farm machinery behave on the road?
source_cards.back: Farm machinery usually has no turn signals, may swing wide left before turning right, and usually travels under twenty-five miles per hour

source_cards.front: What does orange mean on a road sign?
source_cards.back: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols, and the color orange always means road work ahead, slow down.

source_cards.front: What is the fine for speeding where work zone workers are present?
source_cards.back: In Tennessee, speeding in a reduced-speed work zone where transportation or construction workers are present brings a fine of up to five hundred dollars.

source_cards.front: How much time does a work zone sign give at sixty miles per hour?
source_cards.back: A car going sixty miles per hour covers eighty-eight feet per second, so a Road Work one thousand five hundred Feet sign leaves you only seventeen seconds before the work zone.

source_cards.front: When should you merge for a closing lane in a work zone?
source_cards.back: Merge as soon as you learn a lane is closing ahead in a work zone; a last-chance merger can be ticketed and blamed for a crash.

source_cards.front: What should you do before and in a work zone?
source_cards.back: Turn on your headlights before entering a work zone, and do not change lanes inside it unless told to.

source_cards.front: What kind of crash is most common in work zones?
source_cards.back: Most work zone crashes are rear-end collisions, so do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from barriers, equipment and workers.

source_cards.front: What do mobile work zones mean for drivers?
source_cards.back: Mobile work zones such as line painting, patching and mowing mean workers may be ahead even if not yet visible, so heed the signs until you pass the End Road Work sign.
